description: Group C - Perception cost & speed. C1 accessibility-tree snapshot backend selectable via config, producing the same Snapshot/Control[] contract as the DOM walk, benchmarked against domWalk. C2 snapshot diffing (added/removed/changed controls) so the escalation/LLM path can send only the delta and 'N new controls appeared' becomes a first-class overlay/toast event. C3 viewport-priority capture ordering so in/near-viewport controls are surfaced first within the existing ~20 cap. Depends on FEAT-001 config knobs.
steps: C1 a11y-tree backend: in src/snapshot.ts add an alternate capture backend selectable via config.snapshotBackend ('domwalk' default vs 'aria'). Thread the backend into capture() via CaptureOptions.backend (default 'domwalk'). Implement captureAria(page) using Playwright's accessibility snapshot: prefer page.locator('body').ariaSnapshot() (Playwright 1.63 supports aria snapshots) to obtain the ARIA tree, then MAP it into the SAME Snapshot/Control[] contract (ref/index/role/name/tag/type/value/options/editable/checked/disabled + url/title/visibleText + compact text). Because refs must still resolve, stamp data-laya-ref via a follow-up page.evaluate that walks the same accessible elements (role+name) and assigns eN in DOM order, OR resolve aria nodes to elements and stamp them; the key contract is that resolveRef('eN') still works afterward. If a faithful role->tag/type mapping is impossible for some nodes, fill best-effort but keep the contract shape valid. Keep domWalk the default and fully intact. Thread backend from BrowserSession/config so callers (Assist snapshot tool + Autopilot loop capture) can select it; default remains domwalk so existing tests are unaffected.

C1 benchmark: extend test/benchmark/harness.ts (or add a small harness helper) to run the SAME bench cases with backend 'domwalk' vs 'aria' and report per-backend wall-ms and success/coverage, so `npm run bench` (or a dedicated vitest) prints a comparison table. Capture the numbers for the final report. Ensure the aria backend still drives the fixtures to a verified result (or document honestly where it differs).

C2 snapshot diffing: add a PURE function diffSnapshots(prev: Snapshot|undefined, next: Snapshot): SnapshotDiff to a new src/snapshot-diff.ts (or into snapshot.ts). SnapshotDiff = { added: Control[]; removed: Control[]; changed: {before: Control; after: Control}[] } keyed by a stable identity (role+name, since eN refs are per-snapshot). In loop.ts keep the previous snapshot and compute the diff each step. Surface 'N new controls appeared' as a first-class overlay toast/log event when added.length>0. On the escalation path (src/autopilot/escalation.ts), add an OPTIONAL delta-only prompt mode: when a prev snapshot exists and the diff is non-empty and not the first step, build the escalation prompt from the delta (added/removed/changed) plus goal/url/title instead of the full control list, to cut tokens; keep the full-snapshot prompt available and used on the first step or when there is no meaningful diff. Make this behavior additive and covered by a flag/threshold so full behavior remains available.

C3 viewport-priority capture: in the in-page domWalk (src/snapshot.ts), when viewport priority is enabled, order the selected controls so those intersecting or near the viewport (using getBoundingClientRect vs window.innerHeight/innerWidth, within a near-margin) come first, preserving DOM order within each band; keep the monotonic eN assignment consistent with the returned order OR keep eN in DOM order but sort the returned list by viewport proximity - choose one and keep resolveRef correct (eN must map to the element it was stamped on). Thread config.viewportPriority (default true) so the existing ~20-control cap in state-builder.ts then keeps the MOST RELEVANT (nearest viewport) controls. Ensure the ordering is deterministic and does not break existing snapshot tests (if it would reorder existing fixtures' controls in a way a test asserts, prefer keeping eN in DOM order and only reordering the retained/prioritized selection used by buildState, or update the affected assertion minimally while preserving its intent).

Add tests. test/snapshot-diff.test.ts (pure): diffSnapshots detects an added control, a removed control, and a changed control (e.g. value/name change) against a prior snapshot, and returns empty diff for identical snapshots. test/aria-backend.test.ts (real headless chromium): captureAria on a login/search fixture returns a valid Control[] with the expected roles/names and resolveRef('eN') still resolves the stamped elements; optionally assert the loop can run a goal with backend 'aria'. test/viewport-priority.test.ts (real headless chromium): a fixture with an above-the-fold control and a far-below-the-fold control yields the in-viewport control ranked before the far one when viewportPriority is on.
acceptance_criteria: capture(page, {backend:'aria'}) returns a Snapshot with a Control[] matching the existing contract (same fields) and resolveRef('eN') resolves the stamped elements afterward; backend defaults to 'domwalk' and existing behavior is unchanged.

diffSnapshots is pure and correctly reports added/removed/changed controls, with an empty diff for identical snapshots; the loop surfaces 'N new controls appeared' via the overlay when controls are added.
The escalation path can send a delta-only prompt when a diff exists (fewer tokens) while retaining the full-snapshot prompt for the first step / no-diff case.
With viewportPriority on, in/near-viewport controls are ranked ahead of far-offscreen ones within the existing cap; resolveRef remains correct.
A benchmark comparison of the aria backend vs the DOM walk is produced with wall-ms numbers for the report.
verification: Run `npx vitest run test/snapshot-diff.test.ts test/aria-backend.test.ts test/viewport-priority.test.ts` and confirm C1/C2/C3 assertions pass headless.
Run `npm run bench` and capture the domwalk-vs-aria comparison numbers.
Run `npm run test` and `npm run typecheck` and confirm the full suite passes with the 3 pre-existing skips intact.
findings: C1: added captureAria(page) in src/snapshot.ts using page.locator('body').ariaSnapshotJSON({mode:'ai'}) (Playwright 1.63; verified in node_modules/playwright-core/types). It flattens the aria tree to interactive/landmark nodes, resolves each via page.locator('aria-ref=<pwRef>'), stamps our own data-laya-ref='eN' (re-numbered monotonically) and reads faithful tag/type/value/options/editable/checked/disabled off the live element in one evaluate, so resolveRef('eN') resolves the stamped elements. capture() dispatches on CaptureOptions.backend (default 'domwalk'); aria falls back to domwalk if the accessibility snapshot is unavailable. Threaded config.snapshotBackend through snapshotResult (Assist) and runGoal (all per-step/self-heal/VERIFY/final captures). C1 benchmark: extended test/benchmark/harness.ts with runBackendComparison + formatBackendComparison and added a case to report.test.ts, so `npm run bench` prints a domwalk-vs-aria table. Recorded numbers (StubEngine, 4 offline fixtures, headless): both backends 4/4 end-to-end success and 100% mean ops-coverage; domwalk total ~3590-3689ms (~898-922ms/case) vs aria total ~4078-4553ms (~1020-1138ms/case). aria is the slower perception path but faithful on these fixtures. C2: added pure diffSnapshots + hasChanges in src/snapshot-diff.ts (SnapshotDiff type added to src/types.ts) keyed by role+name (eN refs are per-snapshot). loop.ts keeps prevSnapshot, diffs each step, surfaces 'N new controls appeared' as an overlay toast+log when added.length>0 (not on the first step). escalation.ts gained buildDeltaEscalationPrompt + EscalationOptions.diff; loop passes deltaPrompt (server wires deltaPrompt:true) so a non-empty diff on a non-first step sends a delta-only prompt, else the full prompt. C3: domWalk keeps eN stamps in DOM order (resolveRef unaffected) but stable-sorts the RETURNED list by viewport proximity when viewportPriority is on; state-builder's ~20 cap then keeps nearest controls. Threaded config.viewportPriority through capture options. Tests added: test/snapshot-diff.test.ts (7 pure), test/aria-backend.test.ts (4 headless incl. a goal run with backend 'aria'), test/viewport-priority.test.ts (3 headless with a new test/fixtures/viewport-priority.html where the far button is first in DOM but below the fold). Verification: npx vitest run on the three files = 14 passed; npm run bench prints the comparison; full npm run test = 200 passed / 3 skipped (pre-existing skips intact: WebKit smoke + two real-weights autopilot); npm run typecheck + npm run build clean. Everything additive; domwalk remains default. Left package-lock.json untracked per context.json.
